title: Introduce synthetic-load-protector and stable-headroom-allocation to reduce noisy-neighbor regressions
author: Maya R. Chen
description:
Motivation: During several incidents we observed short-lived synthetic/noisy workloads (scheduled internal tests, tenant-side health checks, and 3rd-party probe traffic) causing transient eviction and headroom thrashing in Dedicated fleets. This PR adds two complementary controls: (1) a Synthetic Load Protector that tags and soft-throttles identified synthetic traffic to prevent it from consuming burst/headroom credits; (2) a Stable Headroom Allocation controller that smooths reservation adjustments using a percentile-based decay window to avoid oscillation when autoscaler signals spike.

What this PR does: adds request classification hooks, a synthetic-throttle policy and counter, a headroom allocator that computes reservation deltas using P90/P95 utilization baselines, and new telemetry to report per-tenant synthetic consumption and smoothed headroom allocations. Includes e2e canary rollout plan and migration notes.

Checklist:
- [x] classification + tagging for synthetic traffic (configurable by label and header)
- [x] soft-throttle policy with graceful fallback and tenant opt-out flag
- [x] headroom allocator with percentile decay window and hysteresis
- [x] metrics (synthetic_consumed_tokens, headroom_alloc_smoothed, allocation_delta_histogram)
- [x] unit + integration tests for race conditions and decay logic
- [x] canary rollout job definition and console dashboard tiles

Rollout plan: Deploy controller on dedicated fleet controllers in canary region (us-west-2) for 48h with a 2x synthetic-throttle default. Monitor allocation_delta_histogram and per-tenant SLO signals. If no regressions, expand to rest of dedicated pools over 3 days.

Design notes: Synthetic detection is rule-based and opt-in for now; rules are configurable via fleet policy CRD. Headroom allocator uses a sliding window histogram and applies a decay factor to previous reservation to compute new reservation = clamp(prev * (1 - decay) + forecast * decay, min_headroom, max_headroom). Forecast uses P90 of observed utilization in the window to be robust to short spikes.

Migration and compatibility: Default behavior is a no-op unless fleet policy enables it. Existing autoscaler and burst token pools are left intact; this controller only influences soft reservation deltas and synthetic-tagged requests are excluded from burst accounting when enabled.

feat(allocator): implement smoothed headroom allocation algorithm
test: add unit tests for decay window and race conditions
ci: add canary job and feature flags
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: overall looks good, but please add a concurrency test for the allocator when multiple signals arrive simultaneously. See inline comment in allocator.go: handle potential double-update.
Maya Chen: added a new test allocator_concurrent_update_test and bump to use atomic patching of reservation; addressed race by introducing optimistic compare-and-swap in window_histogram.
Priya Nambiar: Can we avoid discounting short tenant-retries as synthetic? Suggest adding a minimum duration threshold to rule matching.
Maya Chen: implemented min_duration_ms and updated docs; default is 500ms to avoid classifying short retries.
Omar Patel (SRE): CI flaked on e2e in the first run (timeout in canary job). Re-run fixed it; please keep an eye on the canary timeout. Approved after green CI.
ci_history: First CI run: integration timed out (flaky e2e canary). Reran pipeline after test timeout increase and repro fix; second run green.
observability_changes: Adds metrics: synthetic_consumed_tokens{tenant_id}, synthetic_throttle_rate, headroom_alloc_smoothed{pool}, allocation_delta_histogram. Adds Grafana dashboard 'Headroom Stability' with P90/P95 baselines and synthetic overlay.
release_notes: Introduce Synthetic Load Protector and Stable Headroom Allocation: reduces noisy-neighbor eviction and smooths headroom reservations. Opt-in via fleet policy; rollout: canary in us-west-2 followed by global rollout. See docs/runbooks/synthetic-protector.md for configuration.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash. Change set is backwards-compatible and gated by feature flag.
notes_for_changelog: improvement: Add synthetic load protection and smoothed headroom allocator to Dedicated fleet controllers; opt-in via fleet policy. Metrics and dashboard included.
security_considerations: No new auth surface. Policy CRD only configurable by cluster admins. Synthetic tagging respects tenant opt-out and is safe for SSO-managed fleets.
